import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1068

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1068](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1068)
-/

open Cardinal SimpleGraph

namespace Erdos1068

/--
Does every graph with chromatic number $\aleph_1$ contain a countable subgraph which is
infinitely connected?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_1068 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.chromaticCardinal = ℵ_  1 →
      ∃ s : Set V, s.Countable ∧ InfinitelyConnected (G.induce s) := by
  sorry

end Erdos1068

reformulations.difference: Lean asks for an induced subgraph on an at-most-countable vertex set. The cited page asks for a countable subgraph; Bowler–Pitz explicitly require it to be countably infinite.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Adding edges on the same vertex set preserves distinct simple paths and their internal vertex-disjointness. Thus any suitable subgraph yields a suitable induced subgraph, and the converse is immediate. Moreover, InfinitelyConnected includes Nontriviality and requires infinitely many simple paths between distinct vertices. Finite graphs have only finitely many such paths, so this predicate forces infinitely many vertices. Proved the full quantified equivalence to the general-subgraph formulation with both countability and infinitude as Review1068.statement_equiv in /workspace/review/scratch.lean, without sorry.

sources_consulted: N. Bowler and M. Pitz, A note on uncountably chromatic graphs, arXiv:2402.05984v2, especially §4, Remark (3). LaTeX source downloaded from https://arxiv.org/e-print/2402.05984.
review.notes: Checked the sole declaration, answer scope, and referenced definitions. The source still marks the problem OPEN, matching the file. Lean tests verified that chromaticCardinal attains a genuine minimum, that χ(K_V) = #V (making the ℵ₁ hypothesis realizable), that no finite graph is InfinitelyConnected, and that the countably infinite complete graph is InfinitelyConnected. Small-path computations confirmed the internal-disjointness semantics.
